tip: Choosing the best pieces of footage and putting them in order to tell a story.
meaning: Editing is deciding what stays, what goes and in what order, then adding sound, words and effects. It is where a pile of clips becomes a video.
example: From ten minutes of a birthday party you keep a one-minute video of the best moments.

tip: The person, or the program, that edits video.
meaning: An editor is a person who cuts and arranges video. People also call the program an editor.
example: "I am the editor of our school video" means you decide the cuts.
vukem: Vukem Video is an editor that both people and AI agents can use.

tip: The saved file that remembers everything about one video you are making.
meaning: A project keeps your list of clips, where you put them and every change. Your original videos are not changed: the project only points at them.
example: Closing the program and opening it tomorrow, your video is exactly as you left it.
vukem: A [project](/docs/projects) is one JSON document; every change is a batch of operations that raises its revision.

tip: A file you brought into the project: a video, a sound or a picture.
meaning: An asset is any file the project can use. It sits in the library until you put it on the timeline.
example: A song, a photo and three videos are five assets.
vukem: Imported files become assets in the [media library](/docs/guide/media-library).

tip: The shelf where all the files of a project wait to be used.
meaning: The media library lists everything you imported. You pick things from it and drop them on the timeline.
example: Like a toy box: everything is inside, and you take out what you need.

tip: The strip at the bottom of the editor where you arrange clips in time.
meaning: The timeline is a long ruler of time. Left is the start of the video, right is the end. Clips sit on it in the order they are played.
example: Drag a clip to the right and it plays later in the video.

tip: One row of the timeline; clips on the same track play one after another.
meaning: Tracks are rows. A clip on a higher video track is drawn on top of the clips below it. Sound goes on audio tracks.
example: Put a title on the track above your video so the title shows on top of it.
vukem: A track is either visual or audio. See [Tracks, clips and items](/docs/concepts/tracks-clips-items).

tip: One picture stacked above another, like sheets of glass.
meaning: Layers are stacked. What is on top hides what is below, unless the top one is see-through.
example: A drawing of a hat placed over a photo of your face is a layer on top of another.

tip: A piece of video or audio placed on the timeline.
meaning: A clip is a piece of an asset on the timeline. You can make it shorter, move it or split it, and the original file stays the same.
example: From a 5-minute asset you use only 10 seconds as a clip.

tip: Anything on the timeline: a clip, text, a caption, a shape or a sound.
meaning: In Vukem Video, item is the general word for everything you place on a track, whatever its kind.
example: A video clip, a title and a rectangle behind the title are three items.
vukem: Every operation names an `item_id`. See [Tracks, clips and items](/docs/concepts/tracks-clips-items).

tip: The marker on the timeline that shows the moment you are looking at.
meaning: The playhead is a thin line that moves while the video plays. You can drag it to jump to any moment.
example: Put the playhead where the cake appears, then press split.

tip: Dragging the playhead back and forth to look through a video quickly.
meaning: When you scrub, you slide through the video with your mouse, like turning the pages of a book quickly with your thumb.
example: Scrubbing to find the moment the goal happened.

tip: A clock for video, written as hours:minutes:seconds:frames.
meaning: Timecode gives every frame an exact address, like 00:01:30:12. It is how editors talk about an exact moment.
example: "Cut at one minute thirty" is 00:01:30:00.
vukem: Vukem Video writes times like `2s` or `97f`. See [Time](/docs/concepts/time).

tip: The start and the end of the part of a clip that you want to use.
meaning: Set an in point where you want the clip to begin and an out point where it ends. Everything outside is left unused.
example: From a long clip of a swing, you mark the 3 seconds where the kid jumps off.

tip: A flag on the timeline that marks a moment you want to remember.
meaning: A marker is a small flag with an optional name. It does not change the video. It just helps you find a place again.
example: A marker on every beat of a song, to line up the cuts.
vukem: `marker.add`, `marker.set` and `marker.remove`; `M` in the editor. See [Basic timeline editing](/docs/guide/timeline).

tip: Making a clip shorter by moving its start or its end.
meaning: Trimming cuts off the beginning or the end of a clip. You are not deleting the video file, only choosing which part you show.
example: Trim the first two seconds of a clip where nothing happens yet.

tip: Cutting one clip into two at the playhead.
meaning: Splitting puts a cut in the middle of a clip. You get two clips side by side, and you can delete or move either.
example: Split a long clip where the boring part starts, then delete the boring part.

tip: When one change pushes or pulls everything after it, so no gap is left.
meaning: In a ripple edit, if you make a clip shorter, all the clips after it slide to the left to fill the hole. Like pulling a card out of a row and the others close up.
example: Ripple delete a clip and the next clips move closer by themselves.

tip: An empty space on a track where there is no clip.
meaning: A gap shows black (or the layer below) when played. Editors usually close gaps, so the video does not go blank.
example: You delete a clip and a hole is left, a gap, until you close it.

tip: Moving the cut between two clips without changing the total length.
meaning: A roll edit moves the point where one clip ends and the next begins. One clip gets longer and its neighbour gets shorter by the same amount.
example: You want the next shot to appear half a second sooner: roll the cut left.

tip: Moving a clip along the timeline while its neighbours stretch to fit.
meaning: In a slide edit the clip keeps showing the same piece of video, but starts and ends at a different time. The clips next to it get longer and shorter.
example: Slide a short clip a bit to the right so it covers a different moment of the talk.

tip: Changing which part of a clip you see, without moving the clip.
meaning: In a slip edit the clip stays in the same place on the timeline, with the same length, but shows a different part of the original video.
example: A 3-second clip of a jump: slip it to show the moment a little later.

tip: Adding a clip in the middle and pushing everything after it later.
meaning: An insert makes room: the new clip goes in, and what came after moves to the right.
example: Insert a close-up between two shots; the rest of the video becomes longer.

tip: Putting a clip on top of what is there, replacing that part.
meaning: An overwrite covers the old part of the timeline with the new clip. The total length does not change.
example: You overwrite two seconds of the video with a funnier clip.

tip: Clips stick to edges, markers and the playhead when you drag them.
meaning: With snapping on, a clip you drag jumps neatly against the nearby edge, like a magnet, so there is no tiny gap.
example: Drag a title toward the end of a clip and it clicks right at the edge.

tip: Undo takes back your last change; redo puts it back.
meaning: Mistakes are cheap in a video editor. Undo steps back, redo steps forward again.
example: You delete the wrong clip, press undo, and it is back.
vukem: Each person or agent has their own undo history. See [Undo and history](/docs/guide/undo-and-history).

tip: A number that goes up by one every time the project is changed.
meaning: Think of saving a game after every move. The revision is the move number. It lets two helpers know whether the project changed while they were thinking.
example: You and an agent both look at revision 12. You change it, so it is 13. The agent has to look again before changing anything.

tip: A list of edits sent together and applied as one step.
meaning: A batch groups several small changes. Either all of them happen, or none does, so the project is never half-changed.
example: Add a track, put a clip on it and name it, all in one go.
vukem: An `edit` call is a batch. See [Batches, revisions and idempotency](/docs/agents/batches).

tip: Watching your video inside the editor while you work.
meaning: The preview window plays what you have built so far. It may be a little rougher than the final file so it can play fast.
example: You press play to check that the title appears at the right time.

tip: Making the computer build the final pictures of the video.
meaning: Rendering is when the computer works out every frame, with all the layers, colours and effects added, and writes them to a file.
example: After you press export, a bar fills while the computer renders your video.

tip: Putting several clips into one clip, so they act together.
meaning: A nest (or compound clip) is a clip that has its own little timeline inside. You can move or change the whole group at once.
example: Group a photo, a title and music into one block and move the block.

tip: One timeline with a finished or unfinished video on it.
meaning: In some programs a project can hold many timelines, and each one is a sequence. The word also means a run of shots that tell one part of the story.
example: You make one sequence for the trailer and another for the whole video.

tip: Information about a file, such as its length, size or camera.
meaning: Metadata is data about data: the date, the camera, the length of a file. It is not part of the picture.
example: A phone video file knows the time it was recorded.
vukem: `media_inspect` shows an asset's metadata. Text taken from a file is treated as untrusted. See [Safety](/docs/agents/safety).

tip: A project saved as a pattern, with empty places you can fill.
meaning: A template is a finished design where you only swap the picture, the words or the colours, like a form you fill in.
example: A quote card where you change only the quote and the author.

tip: A named empty place in a template waiting for your media or text.
meaning: A slot says: put a picture here, or a name here. Fill every slot and the template becomes your own video.
example: A product teaser template has slots for the product photo and the price.

tip: Your logo, colours and fonts saved once, so every video matches.
meaning: A brand kit keeps the look of a person or a company. Every new video can start with the same colours and fonts.
example: A shop always uses the same orange and the same font in its videos.

tip: Two screens: one shows the original clip, the other the video you are building.
meaning: Many editors have a source window to look at a raw clip and choose the part to use, and a program window to watch the edit.
example: Look at the full clip in the source monitor, mark the best five seconds, then add them to the timeline.

tip: Editing a scene that was filmed by several cameras at the same time.
meaning: When two or three cameras film one event, a multicam edit lets you switch between them, like a TV director.
example: A concert filmed from the front and from the side: you pick the best view moment by moment.

tip: Being able to stop and cut on one exact frame.
meaning: A frame-accurate editor shows the same frame every time you stop on it. That is how you can cut exactly when the ball touches the bat.
example: Cutting on the exact frame where a door shuts.
vukem: The paused preview is the frame that the export produces.
